lines.text: If you eat ice cream too fast,
you might get a sudden, stabbing pain right behind your forehead.
It's called brain freeze, but your brain isn't actually freezing.
When something ice cold touches the roof of your mouth,
it chills the blood vessels running just above it.
and the arteries feeding your brain suddenly widen,
rushing in warm blood to protect it.
But that sudden rush raises the pressure inside your head,
and the nerves there read it as a stabbing headache.
The good news is that it's harmless, and it fades within a minute or two.
And to make it stop even faster,
press your tongue against the roof of your mouth, and warm it back up.
